The four primitives form a cascading diagnostic tree: first, ensure individual gates are obeyed; second, block spurious negative controls; third, validate temporal consistency; fourth, confirm signal validity. Each test is a norm on a specific aspect of system behavior, unified under the StateTransitionNorm framework. Failure modes include systematic drift, leakage, timing errors, and invalid inputs. These operators are designed to be agnostic to internal implementation details, relying only on observable outputs and pre-specified rules. The cross-layer veto conditions enforce that no shortcut can bypass any layer's verification, thereby preventing collinearity and ensuring end-to-end integrity.
